questions.stem: When water boils, what happens to the covalent bonds within the water molecules?

options.text: They become weaker as the temperature increases
They change from covalent bonds to ionic bonds
They remain intact; only the intermolecular forces between molecules are overcome
They break apart, separating hydrogen and oxygen atoms

questions.explanation: When water boils, the covalent bonds within the water molecules remain intact. Only the intermolecular forces between the water molecules are overcome. The water molecules stay as H2O but move apart from each other to become a gas.
